text:
customer_jane: Hi, since last night's rollout our assistant is dropping earlier instructions in sessions >10k tokens. It used to follow a long system prompt but now ignores it halfway through.

support_ash: Sorry about that — can you share a repro (request id or payload)? Any latency/errors?

customer_jane: No HTTP errors. Latency looks normal. Example request id: rid_20260315_7a9f. Conversation was ~12k tokens, system prompt had product rules (do not hallucinate). Model started hallucinating around turn 8.

support_ash: Thanks. Can you paste the raw messages (redact user PII) and the curl you used? Also which model/endpoint you were hitting?

customer_jane: Hitting hosted endpoint model=redwood-m2-large, api_version=2026-03-15. Curl:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-m2-large","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a concise assistant. Follow these rules: ... (long list)"}, {"role":"user","content":"Start conversation..."}, ...], "max_tokens":2048}'
```

customer_jane: Full conversation attached (long). It seems the system prompt gets truncated from the front — the assistant stops referencing rules it previously obeyed.

eng_ben: Tagging infra. We rolled a runtime tweak last night: default context_window cap enforced for some models. Investigating whether it flips trimming policy.

maria_prod: Is this the canary -> global rollout we did at 02:12 UTC? Deploy-bot logs showed: 

```
deploy-bot: rollout redwood-runtime-v1.9 -> canary=10% -> 2026-03-15T02:12:11Z
deploy-bot: canary healthy -> promote -> 2026-03-15T03:45:02Z
```

eng_ben: Looking at request rid_20260315_7a9f in logs: we see a context trim event at 2026-03-15T09:04:22Z: 

```
[info] session=xyz evict_policy=trim_front evicted_tokens=3456 reason=context_cap
[debug] model=redwood-m2-large configured_window=32768 active_window=16384
```

eng_ben: That configured_window mismatch is suspicious — frontend thought 32k, runtime capped to 16k and used trim_front. That would drop the system prefix.

support_ash: If true, that explains the lost instructions. Is this change intended?

alex_ml: Not intended. There was a guard introduced to avoid OOMs that accidentally applied to hosted instances of m2-large. It set runtime active_window=16384 for some routing buckets. Need hotfix to restore 32k for this SKU and ensure trim_back default for chat sessions so that recent user turns are preserved.

maria_prod: Can we prioritize? Customers are hitting production hallucinations. SLA impact likely.

eng_ben: Escalating to exec oncall. Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback runtime v1.9 global promotion, 2) patch routing to set active_window=32768 for known SKUs, 3) change trim policy to trim_back. Rolling patch 2 looks fastest.

support_ash: I told customer we're investigating and asked them to hold traffic if possible. Any quick repro we can run to validate a fix?

eng_ben: Yes — repro script to synthesize long session:

```
# repro.sh
# create 14k-token conversation with long system prompt then user queries
python3 make_long_session.py --system-rules rules.txt --user-turns 12 --send
```

eng_ben: Will deploy patch to routing in ~10m to force active_window=32768 for redwood-m2-large and run repro. I'll post updates.

deploy-bot: patch-routing active_window_override(redwood-m2-large)=32768 -> started

support_ash: Thanks — I'll follow up with customer with ETA.

customer_jane: Appreciate the quick response. We'll pause traffic and try repro after you confirm fix.

alex_ml: After patch we'll also add an assertion in canary that trim_policy==trim_back for chat endpoints; add an alert if runtime cap < model advertised window.

eng_ben: Update: patch applied, repro traffic shows system prompt preserved and no hallucination in 20/20 runs. Monitoring for 30m.

support_ash: Confirmed with customer — they re-ran and saw correct behavior. Closing initial escalation but will keep this thread pinned until we add the assertion. :thumbsup:

maria_prod: Postmortem TODO: - cause analysis (guard rule applied too broadly) - add automated integration test for context window roundtrip - release notes + customer communication - telemetry for evicted_token counts per session

support_ash: Marking follow-ups and assigning to eng-ben + alex_ml.

customer_jane: Thanks team!
